_comment: The effect vocabulary. Every screen and atmospheric effect the game can run is declared here -- its shader, where it composites, what it costs, and every parameter it takes with a type and a default. scripts/world_fx.gd builds nodes from this and NOTHING ELSE, so adding an effect is a shader plus an entry here: no new GDScript, no new node type, no case in a runtime switch.
_ordering: "order" is the compositing order, low first. It is absolute, not authoring order, so two maps that list the same effects in different orders produce identical frames -- which is what makes a screenshot a regression test.
_space: "screen" composites over the finished frame on the fx CanvasLayer, above every world plane and below all UI -- grading must never touch the dialogue box. "world" composites inside the world at a z_index, so a mist can sit behind the foreground trees and in front of the player.
_cost: "reads_screen" effects re-read the frame and cost a backbuffer copy each. This project ships to GitHub Pages under GL Compatibility on whatever hardware a browser is on; scripts/world_fx.gd warns past SCREEN_READ_BUDGET of them. Prefer one grade that does several things to three that each read the screen.
_presets: data/fx/<name>.json holds a named stack a map can ask for by name, exactly as data/lighting/<name>.json does for light. A map may add to or override a preset entry by entry, keyed on "type".

fog._comment: Drifting procedural atmosphere. The mechanism the redwood mist will eventually be a preset of -- deliberately neutral here.

color_grade._comment: Exposure, tint, saturation and contrast over the finished frame.

quantize._comment: Posterizes the frame so 2D light gradients land on a ladder the pixel art can live on. The fix docs/architecture/lighting.md has been waiting for.

vignette._comment: Closes the composition. Costs no screen read.
